title: Conformance matrix, Phase 3 (UPF: N4 PFCP, N3 GTP-U, N6)
note: Same rules as phase1-2-matrix.json: every test reference, function and clause is checked by tools/check/check_matrix.py. verified = tests pass and a real peer or a byte-exact capture confirms it (Open5GS SMF + UERANSIM gNB against our UPF, scenarios S3/S4 with OUR_UPF=1).

rows.procedure: PFCP Heartbeat: answered with our recovery time stamp; our own heartbeats, loss detection after N misses, sessions removed
rows.evidence: Open5GS's SMF exchanges heartbeats with our UPF throughout oracle scenarios S3 and S4.

rows.procedure: PFCP Association Setup initiated by the CP function (Node ID, recovery time stamp, UP Function Features with FTUP and DLBD)
rows.evidence: The real Association Setup Request captured from Open5GS is accepted; the Open5GS SMF associates with the running UPF in S3/S4. Our UP Function Features (FTUP, EMPU) make the SMF ask for CHOOSE F-TEIDs exactly as it does with Open5GS's UPF; claiming the wrong bits made it allocate TEIDs itself, which the differential analysis caught.

rows.procedure: Differential PFCP analysis: the same Open5GS SMF and scenario against Open5GS's UPF and against ours (message sequence and the information elements of every answer)
rows.evidence: The SMF sends an identical request sequence to both UPFs; our Session Establishment and Modification responses match element for element; our usage report carries one extra element (Start Time, allowed by the spec). Captures: tests/fixtures/golden/s3_*.

rows.procedure: PFCP Association Release; peer restart (changed recovery time stamp) removes the peer's sessions
rows.evidence: Sessions are deleted on release, on restart detection and on heartbeat loss; the next association starts clean.

rows.procedure: PFCP Association Update
rows.evidence: Accepted for an established peer; its content (feature changes, graceful release) is not processed.

rows.procedure: PFCP Association Setup initiated by the UP function
rows.evidence: The UPF waits for the SMF to associate (what Open5GS and our planned SMF do); add when an SMF requires UP-initiated association.

rows.procedure: PFCP PFD Management
rows.evidence: Answered with success and ignored: there is no application detection.

rows.procedure: PFCP Session Establishment (PDR, FAR, QER, URR, BAR; F-SEID; Created PDR with allocated F-TEIDs)
rows.evidence: The 596-byte establishment captured from Open5GS is accepted and answered in the same shape (Created PDR for PDRs 2, 3 and 4, shared TEID for the shared choose id); 4 PDRs, 3 FARs, 1 QER, 1 URR, 1 BAR in S3/S4. 41 malformed rule shapes (missing, truncated, duplicated, too many, dangling) are each refused with the right cause and install nothing.

rows.procedure: PFCP Session Modification: update FAR (buffering to forwarding, handover with end marker), create/update/remove rules, Query URR; all-or-nothing
rows.evidence: Open5GS's modification (Update FAR with the gNB tunnel) releases the buffered packet; a modification that fails half-way changes nothing. 29 invalid modifications (unknown or missing ids, dangling references) are refused and leave the session working; valid creates, updates and removes of every rule kind change behaviour as asked.

rows.procedure: PFCP Session Deletion with usage reports in the response
rows.evidence: The usage report (URR id, UR-SEQN, TERMR trigger, times, volume measurement) has the layout of the report Open5GS's UPF sends; counts match the traffic.

rows.procedure: PFCP Session Report: downlink data report and usage report, retransmission (T1 3 s, N1 3)
rows.evidence: Reports are acknowledged by the scripted SMF; an answer of 'session not found' deletes an orphaned session. The oracle SMF's handling of our reports is not exercised by the pinging scenarios.

rows.procedure: Retransmitted requests are answered from a response cache; unsupported versions answered with Version Not Supported
rows.evidence: A repeated establishment does not create a second session.

rows.procedure: Packet detection: F-TEID, UE IP address, QFI, SDF filters (IPFilterRule, with 'assigned'), precedence
rows.evidence: The 'permit out ... to assigned' rule of Open5GS's IPv6 PDR parses and matches; uplink packets are matched against the downlink-oriented rule.

rows.procedure: F-TEID allocation by the UP function (CHOOSE, CHOOSE ID) and release
rows.evidence: Real choose ids and CP-function F-TEIDs from Open5GS.

rows.procedure: Forwarding action rules: forward (towards access with Outer Header Creation, towards core), drop, buffer+notify, end marker on handover
rows.evidence: UE traffic flows through the UPF with Open5GS's SMF and UERANSIM (ping, 0% loss).

rows.procedure: Buffering: BAR limits, notify the CP once, release in order, expiry
rows.evidence: Packet-count and byte limits, age expiry, in-order release.

rows.procedure: QoS enforcement rules: gate status and MBR (token bucket) per QER, shared by PDRs (session-AMBR), QFI marking
rows.evidence: Burst and sustained-rate behaviour measured against the configured MBR. GBR is accepted but not guaranteed (no scheduler).

rows.procedure: GBR enforcement (guaranteed rate)
rows.evidence: Needs a scheduler across flows; belongs with the Stage B datapath.

rows.procedure: Usage reporting rules: volume threshold, time threshold, periodic, immediate (Query URR), final report on deletion
rows.evidence: Counters restart after each report; thresholds apply to the interval.

rows.procedure: UE IP address allocation by the UP function (CHV4 / CHV6)
rows.evidence: Refused with Rule creation failure; Open5GS's SMF and ours allocate UE addresses themselves.

rows.procedure: Multi-access (ATSSS), traffic endpoints, packet duplication, redundant transmission, Ethernet PDU sessions, lawful interception
rows.evidence: Not in the five-NF scope of the plan.

rows.procedure: G-PDU encapsulation and decapsulation with the PDU Session Container (DL PDU session information, QFI)
rows.evidence: A downlink G-PDU produced by our UPF is byte-identical to the one Open5GS's UPF produced for the same packet; the captured uplink G-PDU decapsulates to the original IP packet.

rows.procedure: Echo Request / Response
rows.evidence: Sequence number echoed, Recovery IE returned, over a real socket.

rows.procedure: Error Indication for a G-PDU with an unknown TEID (rate limited)
rows.evidence: TEID data I and peer address IEs; at most 100 per second.

rows.procedure: End Marker sent on path switch (SNDEM)
rows.evidence: Sent to the old tunnel endpoint when an update moves the FAR to a new one.

rows.procedure: N6 through a TUN device to the data network
rows.evidence: Oracle S3/S4 run the UPF on a real TUN device; UERANSIM pings a host behind it (10.99.0.1) with 0% loss.

rows.procedure: NAT / masquerade on N6
rows.evidence: Host configuration (routing and iptables/nftables on the TUN device), documented in deploy/upf/README.md; not done inside the UPF.

rows.procedure: IPv6 UE addresses: /64 prefix session lookup, SDF with 'assigned', source check with link-local exception
rows.evidence: User-plane logic tested with synthetic packets. N3 over IPv6 (Outer Header Creation with IPv6) is refused; no real IPv6 UE in the interop runs.

rows.procedure: Stage A throughput: at least 1 Gbit/s on one host
rows.evidence: Engine alone about 20 Mpps; end to end over real UDP sockets the UPF thread's capacity is 2.3 to 4.9 Gbit/s uplink and 1.4 to 2.2 Gbit/s downlink with 1400-byte packets on this (noisy) host; the gate takes the best of three attempts on capacity per CPU second. The 10 Gbit/s Stage B target needs AF_XDP and a real NIC.

rows.procedure: Robustness: fuzzing of N4, GTP-U and N6 input; ASan, UBSan, TSan
rows.evidence: 1.2 million mutated inputs under ASan+UBSan without a finding; every IE decoder survives every truncation.

rows.procedure: Configuration validated at start-up; health and metrics endpoints
rows.evidence: 27 UPF-specific bad configurations are refused; packet, drop-reason, N4 and session metrics are exported.
